CFML Language Reference: Functions

IIf

Evaluates a Boolean condition. If it is true, the string in the second argument is evaluated as an expression and its value returned; otherwise the third argument is evaluated. It is the inline shorthand for a small CFIF/CFELSE block.

Category

Dynamic evaluation functions

Syntax

IIf(condition, string_expression1, string_expression2)

Parameters

condition
Any expression that yields a Boolean (YES/NO, TRUE/FALSE or a number).
string_expression1
A string holding the expression to evaluate when condition is true.
string_expression2
A string holding the expression to evaluate when condition is false.

Returns

The value of whichever expression was chosen.

Usage

The second and third arguments are strings that are evaluated, which surprises everybody once. To return literal text, wrap it in DE: IIf(Qty GT 1, DE("items"), DE("item")). A bare string such as "items" would be looked up as a variable called items.

Only the chosen string is evaluated, so IIf(IsDefined("Form.Name"), "Form.Name", DE("anonymous")) is safe even when Form.Name does not exist. Do not nest IIf calls inside each other; use CFIF for anything more involved. A popular use is alternating table row colors, as below.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFQUERY NAME="Staff" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets" MAXROWS="6">
SELECT FirstName, LastName, Contract FROM Employees ORDER BY LastName
</CFQUERY>
<TABLE CELLPADDING=3 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR BGCOLOR="#000066"><TH><FONT COLOR="white">Name</FONT></TH><TH><FONT COLOR="white">Status</FONT></TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Staff">
<TR BGCOLOR="###IIf(CurrentRow MOD 2, DE("FFFFFF"), DE("FFFFCC"))#">
  <TD>#FirstName# #LastName#</TD>
  <TD>#IIf(Contract, DE("Contractor"), DE("Employee"))#</TD>
</TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
